desc:
An office has rooms numbered 0..n-1. Each meeting is given as [start, end] and occupies a room for the half-open period [start, end). All start values are different. The meetings are handled in increasing order of start, using these rules:

  • If some rooms are free at the meeting's start, it takes the free room with the smallest number.
  • If every room is busy, the meeting waits for the room that becomes free first (ties: smaller room number). It then starts at that moment and keeps its original length, so its end is shifted by the same delay.
  • A room whose meeting ends at time t is free at time t.

Return the number of the room that hosts the most meetings; if several rooms tie, return the smallest number.

n = 2, meetings = [[0,10],[1,5],[2,7],[3,4]]
[0,10] -> room 0 (until 10); [1,5] -> room 1 (until 5)
[2,7]: both busy, room 1 frees at 5 -> runs 5..10 in room 1
[3,4]: both busy, rooms 0 and 1 free at 10 -> runs 10..11 in room 0
room 0 hosted 2 meetings, room 1 hosted 2 -> tie -> answer = 0
constraints: All start values are distinct (the meetings are not necessarily sorted)
hints: Sort the meetings by start and process them one at a time; delayed meetings only influence the later ones through the room they occupy.
You need two things at each meeting: the free room with the smallest number, and, if there is none, the room that finishes first.

Use a min-heap of free room numbers and a min-heap of busy rooms ordered by (end time, room). Move rooms whose end is at most the start into the free heap. If the free heap is empty, pop the busy heap instead: the meeting starts at that end time, and its new end is that end + (end - start).
editorial: Process meetings by increasing original start; this is the order in which the rules give priority. A meeting that is delayed keeps its length, so we only need to store the (possibly shifted) end time of every busy room.

Free rooms are kept in a min-heap of numbers so that the smallest is chosen. Busy rooms live in a heap keyed by (end time, room number): when everyone is busy, its top is exactly the room that frees first with the smallest number among ties. When rooms are free, first release every busy room with end ≤ start.

Counting the meetings per room and returning the first index of the maximum handles the tie rule. The time is O(m log m + m log n) and the end times can exceed 32 bits in other languages, because delays accumulate, so use 64-bit integers there.
